a significant proportion of RT-qPCR data presented in toxicological studies may be unreliable due to primer design deficiencies.
the bioinformatics workflow presented herein is a useful resource that can be used to identify potential RT-qPCR primer design deficiencies, thus improving the reliability of gene expression data.
the use of bioinformatics tools can help to avoid the publication of potentially erroneous RT-qPCR data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reliability of RT-qPCR data is not guaranteed and should be assessed in a systematic manner.
the quality and reliability of RT-qPCR gene expression data is dependent on the use of high quality primers and RNA samples.
the reliability of RT-qPCR gene expression data should always be considered when evaluating the biological relevance of gene expression changes in toxicological studies.
